title: Traffic Health Protector and Fallback Policy for Automatic Circuit Tripping
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood router needs an automated protection layer that trips soft circuit-breakers and routes requests to fallback model variants or alternate regions when upstream signals indicate overload (429s), elevated timeouts, or growing error rates. Existing guards are manual and coarse; customers see cascading failures during traffic spikes and progressive degradation across regions.

Goal:
Implement a tenant-aware, multi-signal automatic fallback trigger and circuit breaker that: 1) classifies overload vs transient errors, 2) applies graded responses (soft-open -> probation -> hard-open), 3) chooses fallback model variants or lower-tier regions per policy, and 4) integrates with observability and rollback playbooks.

Scope:
- Router decision engine changes: add a Traffic Health Protector (THP) module used by regional and tier routing layers.
- Signals: 429 rate, p99 latency timeouts, 5xx error rate, and probe failures.
- Per-tenant and per-model-variant windows with decay/hysteresis to avoid thrashing.
- Soft-open mode: allow a configurable share of traffic through with probes.
- Probe scheduler and backoff: integrate with existing prober (ENG-612478) for active validation.
- Fallback actions: variant substitution (quantized or cheaper model), route to dedicated capacity, or route to alternate region.
- Observability: create dashboard + automated alerts + incident runbook updates.

Design summary:
- Signals aggregation: sliding windows (60s, 5m) + EWMA to smooth bursts. We compute two derived metrics per (tenant, route, model-variant): 429_rate, timeout_rate (requests with latency > configured SLO), and error_rate_5xx.
- Trip score: linear combination: score = w1*EWM A(429) + w2*EWMA(timeout) + w3*EWMA(5xx) + penalty_if_probe_failed. We map score -> action via thresholds: 
  * score < 0.2 -> healthy
  * 0.2 <= score < 0.5 -> probation (soft-open, reduce to fallback for X% of new requests; start probes)
  * 0.5 <= score < 0.8 -> partial fallback (route new requests to fallback variant or alternate region; keep a small probe stream)
  * score >= 0.8 -> hard-open (evict variant, stop routing except probed health checks)
- Hysteresis & decay: once tripped, apply a decay timer and proportional backoff so recovery requires sustained healthy signals. Use per-tenant cooldown and global safety cap to prevent wide blast radius.
- Soft-open implementation: router will include a probabilistic sampling layer to allow N probe requests per minute and up to p% of normal traffic for gold/tenant. Probes are tagged for tracing.
- Tenant isolation: thresholds and weights are configurable per tenant tier (free, standard, enterprise). Enterprise tenants get more conservative soft-open (lower allowed fail traffic) and faster probes on recoveries.
- Fallback selection: prioritize fallbacks by policy: (1) cheaper local variant -> (2) dedicated pool -> (3) regional failover. Ensure model semantics compatibility via model capability tags.

Implementation steps:
1) Data plumbing (1 sprint): add per-tenant per-variant EWMA metrics into router telemetry stream. Instrument p99 latency and 429 counters. Link to existing metrics pipeline.
2) THP module (1 sprint): implement trip scorer, threshold config, and soft-open evaluator in router.
3) Probe orchestration (half sprint): reuse prober component and add lease-managed probe tokens.
4) Fallback catalog integration (half sprint): map model tags to available fallbacks and implement switch logic with rollback token.
5) Observability & alerts (half sprint): dashboard, SLO alerts, and automated Slack pager for high-impact hard-open events.
6) Canary rollout (1 sprint): enable for internal tenants, then staged customers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Router emits trip events and trip scores to telemetry for every routing decision.
- In synthetic overload test, system elects fallback at score >= 0.5 and reduces error rate for healthy tenants by >= 60%.
- Soft-open behaves as configured: probe traffic < configured cap and is visible in traces.
- Hysteresis prevents flip-flopping under a 2x spike pattern in load tests.
- Observability dashboard surfaces per-tenant trip state and allows filtering by region/tier.

Telemetry & alerts:
- New metrics: thp.trip_score, thp.state, thp.probe_success_rate, thp.applied_action.
- Alerts: trip_score_high (P0), repeated hard-open across regions (P0), probe_failure_rate_high (P1).
- Runbook: document steps to investigate trip source (429 vs timeout), how to force rollback to previous variant, and how to adjust per-tenant thresholds.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag default off.
2) Enable for internal 'redwood-inc' tenant with conservative thresholds.
3) Monitor 72h, tune weights and thresholds, publish runbook.
4) Gradually enable for 10% of customers by usage tier over 2 weeks.
5) Full enable behind tenant opt-in for Dedicated customers.

Rollback criteria:
- If incident shows increasing overall customer errors after enabling THP for a cohort for 30 minutes, immediate rollback to previous routing behavior and alert SRE on-call.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Weight tuning approach: start with simple equal weights and adapt via A/B tests vs ML model to predict cascade risk. A/B adds complexity but may reduce false positives.
- Per-tenant thresholds configuration UX: expose CLI + Console settings or keep in configs managed by platform team?
- Probe cost: probes add request volume; need budget guard for low-tier tenants.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood/SmartRouting/THP-design (draft)
- Prober infra reference: https://confluence.redwood/infra/prober (ENG-612478)
- PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pulls (will link PRs here as they are created)

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on scoring function, hysteresis parameters, and safety caps. We should ensure the default configuration is conservative for public rollout.
